data.name: Dharampal
data.gender_notes: Dharampal is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Dharampal derives from the Sanskrit words dharma and pal. Dharma refers to righteousness, morality, or law. Pal means protector or supporter. Thus, Dharampal is a name that signifies one who upholds righteousness and protects or supports others. The name Dharampal carries the meaning “Dharma (righteousness) + Pal (protector)” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dharampal usually hope their child will grow to embody dharma (righteousness) + pal (protector) and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of moral righteousness and protection.
data.etymology: Dharampal belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Dharma (righteousness) + Pal (protector).”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dharampal total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

Individuals named Dharampal are expected to behave in a just and fair manner, upholding the values of their community and family. This name is also a reminder of the importance of moral character and behavior in Indian culture.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Dharampal signifies a protector and supporter of righteousness and dharma. It represents a deep connection to moral values and the law of the universe. The name carries an inner strength and motivation to uphold truth and righteousness, ultimately leading to a sense of inner peace and fulfillment. It is a reminder that by upholding dharma, one can find protection and guidance in life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dharampal: One who upholds righteousness and duty (Dharma) in life, and strives to maintain spiritual balance and moral values. The name signifies a strong commitment to truth, ethics, and moral principles.

historical_references.reference: In the early 20th century, Dharampal was a prominent Indian nationalist and freedom fighter. He served as the personal assistant to Lala Lajpat Rai, a leading figure in the Indian National Congress. During the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920, Dharampal was arrested for his participation in the civil disobedience movement.

Later in his life, Dharampal became a noted scholar and philosopher, focusing on the spiritual and philosophical traditions of India. He is best known for his work 'The Perfect Harmony: Daily Reflections on the Bhagavad Gita'.
